channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Eleição e bolso: o conceito de 'affordability' que explica por que bons números da economia não garantem votos; ouça 'O Assunto'
item.description: Despite positive macroeconomic indicators in Brazil, many citizens do not feel an improvement in their quality of life due to the concept of 'affordability,' which measures the real ability to cope with the cost of living. Qualitative research identifies three key factors: excessive indebtedness (overdraft, credit cards, consigned loans), consumption frustration (inability to access well-being-associated goods like 'picanha e cerveja'), and hidden spending on online betting (bets), which silently erode household income without clear awareness.

item.title: Messias no STF: relator diz que apresentará relatório favorável ao indicado de Lula em 15 de abril
item.description: Senator Weverton Rocha (PDT-MA), rapporteur for Jorge Messias' STF nomination, said he will present a favorable report in the CCJ on April 15. Messias' confirmation hearing is set for April 29, after the government delivered the official nomination on April 1, ending a standoff with the Senate. He needs at least 41 secret votes in the plenary to be approved.

item.title: Alcolumbre envia indicação de Messias à CCJ e destrava análise; Weverton é definido relator e sabatina será no dia 29
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre forwarded the nomination of Attorney General Jorge Messias to the CCJ, unlocking its analysis for the STF. Senator Weverton Rocha (PDT-MA) was appointed rapporteur, with the hearing set for the 29th. Approval requires at least 41 votes in the Senate plenary, and voting will be secret in both the CCJ and plenary.

item.title: Dino pede vistas em julgamento sobre eleições no RJ; Mendonça antecipa voto
item.description: Justice Flávio Dino requested a view in the STF's judgment on indirect elections in Rio de Janeiro, while André Mendonça anticipated his vote. The case involves two actions determining whether Rio's elections will be indirect (by state deputies) or direct (by popular vote), after a preliminary injunction by Justice Cristiano Zanin suspended the indirect process.

item.title: Líder do PT vê recado de Lula à base ao evitar cravar candidatura à reeleição
item.description: The leader of the PT in the Chamber of Deputies, Pedro Uczai, stated that Lula's declaration that he has not yet decided whether to run for re-election is a calculated strategy to mobilize the party's base and stimulate grassroots engagement, avoiding premature arrogance. According to him, the president is not backing down from candidacy but is respecting internal party processes, such as conventions, and believes victory will depend on political organization, not just government action. Uczai said he has no doubt Lula will be the candidate and sees time to consolidate the government's project despite current low societal mobilization.

item.title: Lula endurece regras em novo pacote contra violência à mulher
item.description: President Lula signed three bills to combat violence against women, including electronic ankle monitors for aggressors, the criminalization of 'vicarious crime' (harming third parties to traumatize women), and the establishment of a National Day for the Protection and Combat of Violence Against Indigenous Women. He stressed that while strict laws are necessary, they alone cannot solve the problem without prevention, criticized the lack of digital regulation and online platforms for enabling violence, and noted that many victims remain silent due to lack of trusted support.

item.title: Flávio Dino pede vista e adia decisão sobre eleições para governador-tampão no RJ
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino requested a view of the cases concerning the election for interim governor of Rio de Janeiro, postponing the decision. The position will govern the state until the end of 2026 following the current governor's departure. The request for a view temporarily halts the judgment at the STF.

item.title: Dino pede vista de julgamento que vai decidir sobre eleição para governo do Rio de Janeiro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino requested a view in the judgment determining whether the Rio de Janeiro gubernatorial election will be direct or indirect following the resignation and cassation of Governor Cláudio Castro. He argued that the court must await the publication of the TSE’s ruling that cassated Castro’s mandate before proceeding. In the meantime, he advocates that the president of the Rio de Janeiro Court of Justice remain in office. Justices Cristiano Zanin and Luiz Fux have already voted: Zanin favors direct popular vote, while Fux supports an indirect election by the state legislature.

item.title: Motta deve escantear medida de Lula para acelerar fim da escala 6×1
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta is expected to prioritize the existing PEC to end the 6×1 work schedule, rather than accept President Lula’s push for an urgent bill on the same issue. Motta’s allies say he will resist Executive interference in the legislative agenda, relying on internal rules that allow PECs to proceed even if the floor agenda is locked. The PEC is set for a vote in the CCJ in the last week of April before moving to a special committee and the plenary.

item.title: Pode ser injusto, mas a maior marca do governo Lula 3 é o caso Master
item.description: Lula's third government is suffering declining popularity due to the Banco Master scandal, with the president attempting to shift blame to the right despite involvement of his allies. The crisis deepens with revelations that Alexandre de Moraes' wife received R$ 80 million from the bank, undermining his anti-Bolsonaro hero image and directly damaging public perception of the administration.

item.title: Dino pede vista e adia julgamento sobre eleição de mandato-tampão no Rio
item.description: Minister Flávio Dino requested a view in the STF judgment on how to elect the temporary governor of Rio de Janeiro following Cláudio Castro's resignation, postponing his vote until the TSE publishes its ruling on Castro's case. The court was tied 1-1, with Cristiano Zanin supporting direct elections and Luiz Fux favoring indirect ones, while André Mendonça urged an early vote due to the vacancy's urgency.

item.title: Justiça do DF condena Gayer por ofensa misógina contra Gleisi
item.description: The Federal District Court of Justice condemned Deputy Gustavo Gayer (PL-GO) to pay a BRL 20,000 indemnity for misogynistic offenses against Gleisi Hoffmann, and ordered a public retraction on social media within ten days. The ruling overturned a first-instance decision, stating Gayer's language was vulgar, sexualized, and devoid of political content. Gleisi and Lindbergh Farias celebrated the decision as a clear message against sexism and political violence.

item.title: Renan Santos admite uso de cogumelos alucinógenos
item.description: Renan Santos, a presidential pre-candidate from the Missão party, admitted to consuming hallucinogenic mushrooms (Psilocybe cubensis) on three occasions, based on leaked Instagram messages from April 2024 to October 2025. He downplayed the impact, stating the use was occasional and in microdoses, and denied it constituted drug trafficking financing, despite his main platform being the fight against narcotics. A criminal complaint filed with the MPF-DF by student Ian Bartholo Lukas Coelho may lead to legal consequences affecting his eligibility.

item.title: Saída antecipada de Cármen Lúcia pegou até ministros da corte de surpresa
item.description: The early departure of Minister Cármen Lúcia from the presidency of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) surprised even other justices, who were not informed in advance of her decision. The move occurred earlier than expected and raised concerns about internal transparency within the body responsible for overseeing elections in Brazil.

item.title: STF retoma julgamento que vai decidir sobre eleição para governo do Rio de Janeiro
item.description: The Brazilian Supreme Court resumed its trial to determine whether the Rio de Janeiro gubernatorial election will be direct (popular vote) or indirect (decided by state legislators), following the resignation and removal of Claudio Castro. Minister Cristiano Zanin voted for direct election, while Luiz Fux supported indirect voting with secret ballot. Justices also agreed on a 24-hour incompatibility period for candidates to resign from current offices.

item.title: Tarcísio aciona Rodrigo Garcia e Vinholi para conter desgaste com prefeitos
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas has appointed former governor Rodrigo Garcia and former regional development secretary Marco Vinholi to mend relations with interior São Paulo mayors, amid complaints of poor communication and reduced state funding transfers. Despite the strain, mayors acknowledge Tarcísio remains electorally competitive due to Bolsonarist support, even without direct reliance on municipal governments.

item.title: Kassab projeta PSD forte no RJ e exalta Paes: ‘Sem acusações de corrupção’
item.description: Gilberto Kassab, national president of the PSD, projected strong party performance in Rio de Janeiro for the 2026 elections, highlighting Eduardo Paes as a competitive and experienced candidate free from personal corruption allegations. He also endorsed Ronaldo Caiado (União Brasil) as a future presidential candidate and emphasized the PSD's Rio strategy will focus on grassroots 'body-to-body' campaigning, despite reduced reliance on physical rallies due to social media.

item.title: Lula: se não obrigar plataformas a cuidarem dos limites internet, não é pai que vai conseguir
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva advocated for social media regulation, urging platforms to be required to control harmful content reaching adolescents, stressing that responsibility cannot fall solely on parents. He made the remarks while signing laws to combat violence against women, linking digital regulation to the protection of vulnerable groups.

item.title: Entre aplausos e vaias, episódio com Flávio revela tom da disputa presidencial
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's appearance at the Chamber of Deputies during the launch of Soraya Santos' candidacy for the TCU revealed the polarized climate expected in the 2026 presidential race. Greeted with both cheers and boos, he responded with gestures like a hand-formed heart while facing chants of 'my president' and criticisms over issues such as 'rachadinha', property purchases, and amnesty. According to columnist Mauro Paulino, this episode directly reflects the confrontational environment candidates will face, with potential for tension escalation—but not violence—and public reaction will be decisive in shaping voter perception.

item.title: PT prepara atos pelo fim da escala 6 x 1 no 1º de Maio
item.description: The PT is preparing a national mobilization for May Day, with events in all 27 states, marches, plenaries, and a digital campaign, centered on ending the 6x1 work schedule. The party will send an urgency bill to Congress to abolish the schedule, coordinated with unions and social movements, as part of its 2026 electoral strategy.

item.title: Pesquisa Real Time Big Data mostra Lula perdendo fôlego em reduto histórico do PT
item.description: A Real Time Big Data poll shows President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s voting intention in Pernambuco has dropped to 56%, about ten points below his 2022 performance, raising concerns for his re-election campaign as the Northeast remains his main electoral base. The decline signals organized right-wing advances in the region, while the PT seeks to expand into traditional opposition strongholds like São Paulo, reflecting a more balanced and nationalized territorial contest ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: TSE retomará julgamento de ex-governador de Roraima na próxima 3ª
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) will resume the trial of former Roraima governor Antonio Denarium (Republicans) on Tuesday, April 14, 2026, over allegations of abuse of political and economic power in the 2022 elections, including the use of public funds in social programs like 'Cesta da Família' and 'Morar Melhor' to boost his re-election. The trial was suspended in November 2025 after a vista request by Minister Nunes Marques and now has two votes already favoring his removal from office. The case was filed by the coalition 'Roraima Muito Melhor', led by the MDB party and Teresa Surita, who received 41.14% of the vote in 2022.

item.title: Lula sanciona leis que endurecem combate à violência contra a mulher e defende controle de redes
item.description: President Lula signed three laws to combat violence against women, including mandatory electronic ankle monitoring for aggressors in life-threatening cases, classifying vicaricide as a heinous crime punishable by 20 to 40 years in prison, and establishing a National Day for the Protection and Combat of Violence Against Indigenous Women. Lula emphasized that laws address symptoms, not root causes, and called for greater investment in education and regulation of digital platforms to counter harmful online content fueling violence.

item.title: Fala de Lula sobre Moraes é vista como estratégia que mira corrida eleitoral
item.description: Lula made a direct appeal to Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, emphasizing his historical trajectory and warning him not to compromise his legacy, particularly regarding the Banco Master case. The statement was seen as a political strategy to distance the government’s image from the STF’s declining reputation, as polls show the court’s wear affects Lula’s prestige directly. Columnist Mauro Paulino argued Lula overreached, attempting to disengage from Moraes despite widespread recognition of his democratic defense role.

item.title: Ministros do STF não querem duas eleições diretas no Rio neste ano; leia bastidor
item.description: STF ministers resist holding two direct elections for Rio de Janeiro's governorship in 2026 due to logistical hurdles, considering alternatives such as an indirect vote in the state legislature or maintaining judge Ricardo Couto as interim governor until December, while keeping the October election for the term starting in 2027. The judgment is underway, with a risk of a tie and potential for a tie-breaking vote by Court President Edson Fachin, though sources deem this unlikely.

item.title: Janja orienta Lula em discurso no Planalto sobre violência contra a mulher
item.description: During a ceremony at the Planalto Palace to sanction a package criminalizing vicaricide and increasing penalties for violence against women, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was corrected by First Lady Janja da Silva when he referred to nearly five thousand people arrested for gender-based violence. Janja intervened to specify that those arrested were 'five thousand men,' which Lula immediately repeated, emphasizing the severity and daily occurrence of gender violence in Brazil. The incident reflects the routine communication adjustments in Lula’s government to avoid gaffes and enhance the precision and impact of presidential speeches.

item.title: STF retoma julgamento de ações sobre eleição de governador no Rio; placar está 1 a 1
item.description: The STF resumed judgment on how to select Rio de Janeiro's new governor after Claudio Castro's resignation, with the vote tied 1-1. Cristiano Zanin favors direct elections, while Luiz Fux supports indirect voting via the state legislature, citing high costs and logistical challenges of holding two elections in under six months. Minister Flávio Dino will open the session, and eight justices remain to vote; the chosen method will determine whether the interim governor is selected by popular vote or by Alerj deputies, serving until December 31.

item.title: Sindicalistas entregam 68 pedidos a Lula na marcha em Brasília
item.description: Union leaders delivered a document with 68 demands to President Lula during a meeting in Brasília. The petition was signed by CUT, Força Sindical, UGT, CTB, NCTS, CSB, Intersindical and Pública. The meeting took place on Wednesday (15) and is part of the government's ongoing dialogue with labor organizations.

item.title: Lula sanciona pacote que cria crime de vicaricídio e aumenta penas para violência contra a mulher
item.description: President Lula signed a package of laws to combat domestic violence, including the creation of the crime of vicaricide, mandatory electronic ankle monitoring for aggressors, and increased penalties. The law also establishes a national awareness day and expands protective measures, such as alert devices for victims and authorization for delegates in cities without judges.

item.title: PSD muda de posição e passa a ser contra voto secreto em eventual eleição indireta para governo do Rio
item.description: The PSD reversed its stance on secret voting in a potential indirect election for Rio’s governor, now advocating for open voting at the STF. The shift came after Eduardo Paes’ allies acknowledged they would likely lose in the Alerj even with secret voting, as shown by a March test vote for Alerj president where Douglas Ruas (PL) won 45 votes before the result was annulled.

item.title: Cinco pré-candidatos à Presidência terão que ser convidados para debates na TV
item.description: Five pre-candidates for the presidency will have the mandatory right to participate in TV and radio debates during the 2026 election campaign, should they confirm their candidacies: President Lula (PT), Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), former governors Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) and Romeu Zema (Novo), and writer Augusto Cury (Avante). The obligation stems from the closure of the party window and current electoral regulations.

item.title: Bastidores: Base de Lula teme perda de veto em PEC 6x1 e pressiona por projeto
item.description: Lula's government base fears losing presidential veto power if the 6x1 workweek reform is approved via constitutional amendment (PEC), as PECs are not subject to presidential veto. At the same time, there is concern that sending a bill with constitutional urgency could strain relations with House Speaker Hugo Motta, risking rejection or being struck down as unconstitutional by the Supreme Court.

item.title: TSE oculta CPF de candidatos e dificulta fiscalização
item.description: The TSE has made concrete progress in electoral transparency through public hearings and electronic voting machine tests, but maintains a decision to hide candidates' CPFs, hindering oversight and needing reversal before the 2026 elections.

item.title: STF AO VIVO – Formato da eleição tampão para governador do Rio de Janeiro – sessão 9/4/2026
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court resumed proceedings on the format of the interim election for governor of Rio de Janeiro, with Minister Luiz Fux supporting indirect elections and Cristiano Zanin advocating for direct voting. The Court also resumed judgments on ADI 6553 regarding the reduction of Jamanxim National Park and the Ferrogrão railway, a Google appeal concerning data privacy in the Marielle Franco case, and two ADPFs challenging the TCU’s Secex-Consenso unit and the Ferrari Law on free enterprise grounds.

item.title: Manipulação de apostas caiu 80% no Brasil, diz diretor da Sportradar
item.description: Felippe Marchetti, Director of Integrity Partnerships at Sportradar in Brazil, said sports betting manipulation cases dropped by about 80% over the last three years, falling from 150 suspicious cases in 2022 to just 8 identified by April 2026. He credited the regulation of Brazil’s betting market for improving information sharing among operators, government, and integrity bodies, and noted that Sportradar monitors over 10,000 Brazilian football matches across state and national leagues.

item.title: Comissão aprova prioridade para mães de pessoas com deficiência em programas de emprego
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies' Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities approved Bill 114/26, which prioritizes unpaid caregivers of people with disabilities — especially mothers — in federal employment and productive inclusion policies. The bill amends the National Employment System (Sine) and the Acredita no Primeiro Passo program to promote financial autonomy for caregivers, recognizing the social value of unpaid care work. Reporter Duarte Jr. (Avante-MA) emphasized that caregiving responsibilities, disproportionately borne by women, hinder labor market entry, and the bill now proceeds to the Committees on Labor and Constitution and Justice.

item.title: Tribunal endossa decisão do TRE-AC que condenou Hildebrando Pascoal
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) upheld the conviction of former federal deputy Hildebrando Pascoal Nogueira Neto for electoral corruption and related crimes in the 1998 elections, rejecting the defense's criminal revision requests. The TRE-AC's sentence of 14 years in prison and a fine was fully maintained by the TSE justices, with rapporteur Minister Estela Aranha dismissing claims of judicial bias, lack of police inquiry oversight, and double punishment. The ruling had already become final and unappealable in 2004.

item.title: Cármen Lúcia anuncia saída antecipada da presidência do TSE
item.description: Minister Cármen Lúcia announced she will step down from the presidency of the TSE on April 14, earlier than her scheduled term end on June 3, to ensure administrative calm ahead of the October general elections. The election for TSE president and vice president will take place next Tuesday, with Kassio Nunes Marques as the natural successor and André Mendonça as vice.

item.title: O companheiro Alexandre
item.description: President Lula expressed concern about the image of Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, stating that Moraes is aware his actions harm his public image. Lula revealed he gave Moraes advice during a Wednesday, January 8 interview.

item.title: Moraes manda tirar de inquérito pedido de Linbergh para investigar Moro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered the removal of a request by federal deputy Lindbergh Farias (PT-RJ) to investigate Senator Sergio Moro over alleged implications about the legitimacy of Lula's 2022 election, following the PGR's opinion that only the Public Prosecutor's Office can initiate criminal proceedings against legislators. The request was deemed extrajudicial and thus inadmissible in the digital militias inquiry.

item.title: Sucessão no Rio: julgamento no STF é termômetro para futuro político de Cláudio Castro
item.description: The STF's judgment on the Rio de Janeiro gubernatorial election examines whether Cláudio Castro's (PL) resignation was a maneuver to avoid TSE-imposed cassation, already deemed a fraud by ministers like Zanin and Gonet. Although not formally removed, Castro faces the effects of ineligibility until 2030, threatening his Senate ambitions. Early signals from the STF suggest an unfavorable climate for the former governor, including potential liability for the costs of the indirect election.

item.title: Eleição do TCU vira teste de força de Motta dentro da Câmara
item.description: The election of the new TCU minister has become a test of strength for House President Hugo Motta, who is working to secure the election of Odair Cunha as part of an agreement with the PT. Centrão and opposition parties have fielded alternative candidates to challenge the Planalto Palace, but Motta is targeting first-term lawmakers to ensure support. A negative outcome for Odair Cunha would not only break Motta’s promise but could also damage his credibility as House leader.

item.title: Cármen Lúcia antecipa saída da presidência do TSE
item.description: Minister Cármen Lúcia advanced the succession election for the TSE presidency to April 14 to prevent administrative disruptions during the 2026 General Elections organization. Minister Kassio Nunes Marques is expected to assume the role, allowing more time for team appointments and planning. Cármen Lúcia will remain a TSE minister until August but may leave the Court after the transition.

item.title: TSE mantém condenação de deputado de Roraima por compra de votos
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) upheld the cancellation of the mandate of state deputy Renan Bekel (Republicans-RR) for vote buying in the 2018 elections, confirming the 50,000 Ufirs fine imposed by the Roraima Regional Electoral Court (TRE-RR). The unanimous decision was based on robust evidence, including phone interceptions and messages, which revealed a structured scheme of payments to electoral operatives (R$250) and voters (R$100) to secure votes.

item.title: Plenário confirma extinção de ação contra prefeito de Riachinho (MG) por falha processual
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court unanimously upheld the dismissal of an action against Riachinho's mayor, Neizon Rezende da Silva, due to a procedural error: the plaintiff coalition failed to include the vice-mayor candidate in the defendant list within the legal deadline, rendering the case invalid from the outset. The ruling preserves the mayor and vice mayor's mandates, overturning the initial conviction.

item.title: Cotado para palanque de Flávio em MG, Cleitinho se indispõe com bolsonaristas
item.description: Senator Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos-MG), tipped as a potential candidate for Flávio Bolsonaro in the 2026 Minas Gerais gubernatorial race, sparked controversy after criticizing Donald Trump’s remarks about Iran, warning that Trump’s rhetoric risked mass civilian casualties and a potential third world war. His comments drew backlash from Bolsonaro supporters who regard Trump as a key international leader of the movement, while congressman Otoni de Paula (PSD-RJ) defended him, accusing critics of blind, selective loyalty to Trump.

item.title: Cármen Lúcia convoca eleições no TSE e antecipa transição para Nunes Marques
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Cármen Lúcia announced her early departure from the presidency of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) and called for elections on April 14 to choose her successor, Minister Nunes Marques, following seniority rules. The move aims to ensure a smooth transition and preparedness for the October 2026 elections, as Nunes Marques and André Mendonça — both appointed by Bolsonaro — are set to assume the TSE presidency and vice-presidency. Although formal, the election is procedural, as succession follows strict seniority among STF ministers.

item.title: Em jantar sem Alcolumbre e com Zanin, Messias se reúne com senadores e reforça busca de votos ao STF
item.description: The Attorney General of the Union, Jorge Messias, attended a dinner with senators in Lago Sul, Brasília, to strengthen his lobbying for a Supreme Federal Court (STF) seat, with Justice Cristiano Zanin present and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre absent. The meeting aimed to map votes and deploy arguments such as the risk of a 'worse' nominee if Messias is rejected, while also discussing the presidential veto on sentencing guidelines for January 8 acts as a tool for political pacification. Despite growing support, Messias has not yet secured the 14 votes required for Senate approval.

item.title: Master: Ao inocentar Campos Neto, Galípolo contrariou estratégia combinada no Palácio do Planalto
item.description: Gabriel Galípolo, president of the Central Bank, defied a coordinated Planalto strategy by exonerating Roberto Campos Neto from blame in the Master scandal during his testimony before the Organized Crime CPI. The strategy, agreed upon in a March meeting with Lula and ministers Rui Costa, Sidônio Palmeira, and Fernando Haddad, aimed to hold Campos Neto accountable. Galípolo’s deviation has created tension within the government amid the ongoing crisis.

item.title: Cármen Lúcia antecipa saída do TSE e marca eleição de Nunes Marques para semana que vem
item.description: Minister Cármen Lúcia, president of the TSE, announced her early departure from the court's presidency and scheduled the election of her successor, Kassio Nunes Marques, for next week (day 14). She stated the move aims to ensure balance and administrative tranquility during the electoral period, avoiding a leadership change too close to the 2026 elections. The transition will be carried out with future vice-president André Mendonça, with the new leadership's inauguration expected in May.
